title: Nkatenkwan with Okra and Eggplant
author: Yaa Darko
desc: The version with vegetables in it — two cups of okra and a whole eggplant added five minutes after the main pot, cooked until chicken and vegetables are tender.
longDesc: Most documented groundnut soups are meat and peanut alone. This one puts the vegetables in the pot: two cups of chopped okra and a medium eggplant go in five minutes after the main pot is assembled, and everything cooks until both the chicken and the vegetables are tender. Two thirds of a cup of peanut butter to one chicken is the leanest peanut ratio of any documented version, which makes this the thinnest and most broth-like of the family — closer to light soup with groundnut in it than to the thick diaspora versions.
steps: Assemble the chicken, ginger, half onion, tomato paste, peanut oil, chopped onion, chopped tomatoes, peanut butter, salt and chiles in the pot.
Add the eggplant, cut into chunks, and the chopped okra.
Cook until the chicken and vegetables are tender.
chefTips: Two thirds of a cup of peanut butter to a whole chicken is the leanest documented ratio. Expect a broth rather than a thick soup — that is this version, not a mistake.
Vegetables in after five minutes. They are part of the soup here rather than a side, which no other documented groundnut soup does.
Okra will thicken the soup slightly as it cooks and releases its mucilage. Two cups is a lot, so the body comes partly from the okra rather than the peanut.
Until chicken and vegetables are tender is the only cue. Unusually, this recipe does NOT mention the oil separating, which every other documented version treats as essential.
Eggplant in chunks, not slices. It will collapse if cut too small.
Two hot chiles or a teaspoon of cayenne — the source offers either, and they are not equivalent in flavour.
If you want the standard thick nkatenkwan, this is not the recipe. Start at GHA013.
commonMistakes: Expecting a thick soup from this peanut ratio.
Adding the vegetables at the start.
Cooking it so long the okra disintegrates.
Assuming the oil will separate as in the other versions — this recipe does not call for it.
sources: Adapted from 'Hkatenkwan (Groundnut Stew)' in the Africa News Cookbook material as compiled in 'Recipes from Ghana', credited on the page to 'From Carol Miller-Tutzauer, University at Buffalo', dated Friday 13 September 1991, hosted at africa.upenn.edu. ATTRIBUTION FLAG: the compilation credits several published cookbooks collectively and the credit for this specific entry is not explicit, so the compilation is cited rather than an individual author. The spelling 'Hkatenkwan' is as printed — almost certainly a typesetting error for 'Nkatenkwan', and it is reproduced rather than silently corrected.

Ingredients exactly as printed: Chicken (1, cut up); Ginger (1-inch piece); Onion (½); Tomato paste (2 tbsp); Peanut oil (1 tbsp); Chopped onion (1 cup); Chopped tomatoes (1 cup); Peanut butter (⅔ cup); Salt (2 tsp); Hot chiles (2, or 1 tsp cayenne); Eggplant (1 medium); Okra (2 cups).

Method as printed: main pot 5 minutes before the vegetables go in, then cook 'until chicken and vegetables are tender'. No yield is printed; the five servings above is an editorial reading of one whole chicken and is labelled as such.

NOTABLE OMISSION, and the reason this version is published separately: this recipe does NOT give oil separation as an endpoint, where every other documented groundnut soup does. Its only cue is tenderness. That absence is recorded rather than filled in from the other sources.
THE OKRA AND EGGPLANT are also unique to this version among the documented groundnut soups, and they change what the dish is — the okra's mucilage supplies body that the low peanut quantity does not.
PEANUT RATIO POSITION: ⅔ cup peanut butter to one whole chicken is the leanest of the six documented versions. For the full fivefold spread see the sources at GHA013.

A SOURCING CAVEAT ON THIS COMPILATION: it is a 1991 university-hosted gathering of recipes from named published cookbooks, which is a weaker provenance than a bylined recipe. It is used here because it carries complete quantities and because its vegetable treatment is not documented anywhere else. The same compilation's fufu entry — Bisquick and instant potato flakes — is explicitly rejected at GHA001, so the collection is treated as uneven rather than reliable throughout.
storage: 3 days refrigerated. The okra softens further.
reheating: Gentle heat. Do not boil hard or the okra breaks down.
healthBenefits: Okra supplies soluble fibre, folate and vitamin K.
Eggplant adds fibre and anthocyanins in the skin.
The leanest peanut ratio of the documented versions, so lower in fat.
High in protein from the whole chicken.
culturalNote: Putting okra and garden egg into groundnut soup is closer to how it is actually eaten in many Ghanaian households than the meat-and-peanut versions that get published — the vegetables stretch the pot and the okra does some of the thickening work the peanut would otherwise have to do alone.
